identity.title: A multiwavelength analysis of the spiral arms in the protoplanetary disk around WaOph 6

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first near-infrared polarimetric observations of WaOph 6 obtained with SPHERE at the VLT and compare them to archival millimeter continuum ALMA observations.

evidence.quote: WaOph6 is a K6 star (cite: Eisner2005), and member of the Ophiuchus moving group at a distance of 122.5 $^{+0.3}_{-0.2}$ pc (cite: Gaia2020)

question.value: What is the morphology of the WaOph 6 disk in NIR scattered light versus ALMA mm continuum, and can a planetary perturber explain the spiral arms?

evidence.quote: We aim to perform an in-depth characterization of the protoplanetary disk morphology around WaOph 6 analyzing data obtained at different wavelengths, as well as to investigate the origin of the spiral features in the disk.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: [ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00484.L]
WaOph 6 was observed within ALMA/DSHARP (cite: Andrews2018) in Band 6, at a frequency of 239 GHz (1.3 mm).

analysis_steps.goal: Trace spirals in ALMA and SPHERE data

method.value: Peak search along radial direction on tclean images (3 sigma) and peak_local_max on deprojected polar SPHERE image

evidence.quote: Then, we searched for peak emission points along the radial direction and took the 3$\sigma$ emission ones as the spiral arms.

method.value: Logarithmic and Archimedean spiral models fitted with emcee, i and PA fixed

evidence.quote: To test the symmetry of the spiral arms, the parameters $r_0$ and $b$ were fitted separately, while we assumed $i$ and PA to be fixed
we used 250 walkers with two consecutive burning stages of 1000 and 500 steps, and then 1500 steps to sample the parameter space.
A flat prior probability is used for the free parameters.

analysis_steps.goal: Hydro + radiative transfer test of planet perturber

method.value: PLUTO 3D gas and FARGO3D 2D gas+dust simulations, then RADMC-3D and CASA simobserve/tclean synthetic ALMA images

evidence.quote: we performed 3D gas-only and 2D gas+dust hydrodynamical simulations in which a massive planet at a separations $\geq 90$ au generates large-scale spiral arms interior to its orbit.

The obtained images resemble the ones detected both in the scattered light and millimeter continuum observations, except for the fact that we are only able to fit either the inner or the outer spirals

claims.hypothesis: Spiral arms are driven by a planet rather than GI
claims.experiment: Toomre Q estimate and hydro+RT simulations
claims.result: Q>2.2 everywhere; 10 MJup planet at 140 au reproduces spirals
claims.finding: A planet of at least ~10 MJup could drive spirals

evidence.quote: we find that a planet of minimum 10 M$_{\rm{Jup}}$ outside of the observed spiral structure is able to drive spiral arms that resemble the ones in the observations
